standalone_note: None. Every kept place lies inside Canberra's span (40 km, 30 km at 75%) or Namadgi's (50 km, 37.5 km), and is reached from that base. There is no ACT land outside both that holds a kept place.

tidbinbilla_decision.considered: Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve as its own destination (a headline attraction with Wikipedia and VisitCanberra billing, so it passes the name test).
tidbinbilla_decision.rejected_because: Only three kept places belong to it: Gibraltar Peak (inside the reserve), the Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex and the reserve itself. Gibraltar Falls is on Wikivoyage's Namadgi page and Corin Forest is on Corin Road beside Namadgi, so they are Namadgi spots. Two or three never make a destination. The reserve (25 km), the peak (23 km) and the complex (19 km) are inside Canberra's 30 km reach and are reached from the city, so they are Canberra spots.
tidbinbilla_decision.owner_can_revisit: If the owner wants a Tidbinbilla pin, Gibraltar Falls and Corin Forest would have to move out of Namadgi to reach four.

span_overlap_note: Canberra (centre -35.2976, 149.1013, 30 km reach) and Namadgi (centre -35.5313, 149.0658, 37.5 km reach) are 26 km apart, so their spans overlap at the fringe (Tharwa, Lanyon Homestead). The overlap holds no shared spot: Lanyon Homestead (Tuggeranong, 24 km from the Canberra centre) is reached from the city, Tharwa is Namadgi's gateway at its visitor centre.
existing_fixes_note: The ACT has no destinations or spots in src/data. Goulburn and Batemans Bay (NSW standalone spots) are outside this region.

review.name: Glebe Park
review.reason: Wikivoyage Civic names it as a pleasant stroll and an autumn-colour photo spot (one counted source); 40 ha? urban park. Case for: a guide singles it out, free, open always. Case against: an ordinary city-centre park, one source, short visit.
review.objection: Run rule rejects urban parks no guide singles out; Wikivoyage does single it out but only in one sentence.

review.name: Canberra Merry-Go-Round
review.reason: Wikivoyage Civic lists a heritage-listed 1914 carousel (52 carved horses, mechanical organ, $3 a ride, set daily hours) in a permanent pavilion on City Walk. Case for: heritage landmark, permanent. Case against: a ride of a few minutes, one source, a short visit, an operated amusement.
review.objection: Rule rejects operators and rides; here the carousel is a heritage object in a fixed place, but a $3 ride is about 5 minutes.

review.name: Canberra City Art Trail
review.reason: VisitCanberra museums page names a self-guided walk through the city centre passing iconic installations. Case for: a named agency walk, free, always available. Case against: one counted source, a route of scattered artworks not a single place, no list of stops in hand.
review.objection: A trail is a route not a spot, and the installations are individually minor.

review.name: Tuggeranong Art Trail
review.reason: VisitCanberra names a family-friendly self-guided art trail in Tuggeranong with short drives and easy walks. Case for: agency-named, free, permanent. Case against: one counted source, aimed at kids, a scattered route with no single destination.
review.objection: Same objection as the City Art Trail, plus weaker billing.

review.name: Captain James Cook Memorial
review.reason: VisitCanberra attractions and 100-things lists name this lakeside water jet and globe (counted, read); a landmark guides single out beside Lake Burley Griffin, but a lakeside memorial that is a short stop; the jet runs only at set hours.
review.objection: For: two counted sources, a distinctive landmark visitors photograph at Regatta Point. Against: a memorial and a short visit, with the jet not always running; Wikivoyage Civic treats Civic memorials as not popular destinations.

review.name: Australian-American Memorial
review.reason: Wikivoyage North Canberra calls it the only sight of interest at Russell Offices (the main Canberra page names it too): a tall column visitors can walk to. Case for: a landmark visible from the lake axis, free, always open. Case against: a minor memorial, a short stop, set in a defence office area.
review.objection: Brief rules minor memorials out unless a source singles them out; Wikivoyage does single this one out as the only sight there.

review.name: Mount Pleasant Lookout
review.reason: Mount Pleasant Lookout: Wikivoyage North Canberra lists it (Artillery memorial with two cannons, Gen. Bridges grave, view over Duntroon); parks agency has a reserve page. Short stop. Case for: two counted sources, a drive-up lookout with things to see. Opened Wikivoyage.
review.objection: A 10-20 minute roadside pull-out with a modest memorial; the listing has a dead link and a guide does not single it out as a headline view.

review.name: Classics Museum
review.reason: ANU Classics Museum: Wikivoyage Acton lists it (Mon-Fri 9-6, ancient Greek and Roman artefacts, also Indigenous displays in the A.D. Hope Building), free and open. Case for: a real small museum; against: one source, university corridor, weekdays only, short visit. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
review.objection: The collection is small and inside a university building, so a visitor from elsewhere would not go out of their way.

review.name: Drill Hall Gallery
review.reason: Drill Hall Gallery: Wikivoyage Acton lists it (Wed-Sun noon-5, free, Sidney Nolan's Riverbend displayed at the front); ANU gallery with rotating contemporary exhibitions. Case for: open, free, a permanent Nolan; against: one source, temporary exhibitions. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
review.objection: Rotating shows mean there is no fixed thing to see, and one source names it.

review.name: Shine Dome
review.reason: Shine Dome: Wikivoyage Acton calls it a landmark since the late 1950s nicknamed the 'martian embassy', but gives no hours or interior; the case for is a photographed modern icon, against that it is exterior-only (rule 2) unless a tour exists. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
review.objection: Seen from the street and the Academy runs public tours rarely, so it fails rule 2 as a building only seen from outside.

review.name: Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies
review.reason: AIATSIS: Wikivoyage Acton lists it (Mon-Fri 9-5) as somewhere to learn Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander culture, with public exhibits and a library. Case for: cultural stop with a source; against: a research institute whose public exhibits are modest and one source. Opened Wikivoyage Acton.
review.objection: It is primarily a government research institute and library, and the draw to a traveller is unclear.

review.name: Canberra Fire Museum
review.reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage South Canberra lists restored fire appliances, free entry; but open Saturday 10-14 only.
review.objection: Open one morning a week and a small volunteer museum, so it is not there whenever you arrive; one source only.

review.name: Gossan Hill
review.reason: Rule 1/2: ACT Government walks list (act.gov.au Feb 2026 'great Canberra walks') names a 2.5 km loop in a 47 ha nature reserve; Ginninderry and HerCanberra describe it as a short walk with views.
review.objection: Short walk, one government list source, no distinct lookout confirmed; the lengths disagree (1.7 vs 2.5 km). Cannot open the agency page.

review.name: Hall School Museum and Heritage Centre
review.reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Hall lists the local museum in the former primary school (bush school history).
review.objection: Open Thursday mornings and Sunday afternoons only, small, one source; not there whenever you arrive.

review.name: Bridge to Bridge Loop
review.reason: Rule 1/3: Visit Canberra 100 things names the 5 km walk past the War Memorial and Parliament House; locals' favourite.
review.objection: It is a route around parts of Lake Burley Griffin and passes sights listed on their own (War Memorial, Parliament House), so near-duplicate of the lake; one counted source.

review.name: Evatt Wetlands and Ginninderra Creek Trail
review.reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Belconnen describes an eco-restored creek reserve with wetlands and trail, free car park.
review.objection: Local nature trail with one source; may be part of the Lake Ginninderra area; not a headline walk.

review.name: John Knight Memorial Park
review.reason: Wikivoyage Belconnen lists the 12 ha lakeside park with the 'Snake House' play structure, water garden, free barbecues (opened); not a memorial.
review.objection: Against: local family park. For: guide names several features.

review.name: Umbagong District Park Grinding Grooves
review.reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Belconnen names the protected Aboriginal grinding grooves site in the creek bed, open 24 hours.
review.objection: Small site, one source, could be a short stop; sensitive heritage visit not obviously signposted.

review.name: Cooleman Ridge
review.reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Canberra names it among popular bushwalking destinations within the urban parks; reserve with tracks.
review.objection: Only a name in a list, no detail of what to see; coordinates missing; one source.

review.name: Mugga-Mugga Cottage
review.reason: Wikivoyage lists a 1830s cottage open 10-2 on the first weekend of each month only, so it is not there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4).
review.objection: Case for: three counted sources, genuine heritage house. Against: opens one weekend a month.

review.name: Tuggeranong Schoolhouse Museum
review.reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage lists the 130-year-old schoolhouse with pastoral-era furniture.
review.objection: Open only the second Sunday of the month, link dead, one source.

review.name: Geoscience Australia
review.reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong: education centre of minerals, rocks, fossils, free, weekdays 9-5.
review.objection: Government agency visitor centre, weekdays only, one source; a short visit.

review.name: Tuggeranong Arts Centre
review.reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong and Country ACT list galleries and a theatre, Tue-Sat.
review.objection: Local arts centre mostly a theatre and studios; mostly events, one dead-link listing.

review.name: Lake Tuggeranong
review.reason: Only Wikivoyage's Tuggeranong pages (one family) name it: 'nice small walk around the lake', otherwise somewhere to sit. One source family, short visit.
review.objection: Case for: a named district lake with a walk. Against: an urban amenity lake, not a trip.

review.name: Sparrow Hill and East Kowen Forest Trails
review.reason: Wikivoyage names the trailhead for mountain biking and hiking in a pine plantation (rule 1), a legitimate activity place.
review.objection: One source; a commercial plantation trail network, not a distinct landmark; Kowen Forest may be better covered by another candidate.

review.name: Lindsay Pryor National Arboretum
review.reason: Wikivoyage Woden lists it twice (Woden and Weston Creek pages): lakeside arboretum good for autumn colour and a stroll (rule 1, 2).
review.objection: Wikivoyage itself notes poor maintenance, it is the former arboretum, and it is near-duplicate in kind to the National Arboretum; a stroll only.

review.name: Scrivener Dam
review.reason: Wikivoyage has a viewing platform off Lady Denman Drive at the dam that created the lake; a short stop beside the zoo, named in several listings but a quick look (rule 3).
review.objection: Case for: five counted sources and named by Wikivoyage. Against: a 10-minute roadside lookout beside the zoo.

review.name: Stromlo Cottage
review.reason: Wikivoyage Woden and the Weston Creek page both list a 1926 heritage cottage that tells Canberra's story (two counted sources). Opened Woden page.
review.objection: Wikivoyage entry dates from 2022 and gives no hours or confirmation that it is open to visit; a small suburban cottage.

review.name: Parliamentary Triangle
review.reason: Precinct that contains Parliament House, High Court, National Gallery, Archives and others already candidates here; overlaps (run rule). Wikivoyage names it as the heart of Canberra sightseeing.
review.objection: Case for: a guide frames it as one walk. Against: duplicates its member institutions.

review.name: Manuka Pool
review.reason: Wikivoyage South Canberra lists an art deco 1930 pool; heritage character and a swim (rule 2). Opened that page.
review.objection: Open only late October to mid-March; one source; essentially a local pool.

review.name: Yarralumla Bay
review.reason: Lakeside bay named by VisitCanberra's attractions list (opened); second-tier lake foreshore with a paddle hub but no named thing to see beyond the shore.
review.objection: One source, thin description, no coordinates, may be a local foreshore.

review.name: Craft and Design Canberra
review.reason: Craft and design gallery (The Treasury) named on two VisitCanberra pages (opened); public gallery, free entry likely, but small.
review.objection: Contemporary craft gallery and shop; short visit, little draw beyond Glassworks.

review.name: Gallery of Small Things
review.reason: Quirky 'smallest gallery' in Watson, two VisitCanberra pages plus Wikivoyage; opens Thu-Sun only.
review.objection: Wikivoyage calls it an art shop; limited hours, far north suburb.

review.name: Kings Park
review.reason: Wikivoyage (opened) gives Kings Park a section with six memorials and the Griffin plans; the National Capital Exhibition is the visit and may be its own candidate.
review.objection: Mostly minor memorials; a park of lawns beside Commonwealth Park; one source.

review.name: Red Rocks Gorge
review.reason: Murrumbidgee gorge named by the parks agency pages (parks-act-leads list, relied on) and a walking guide; walk between Kambah Pool and Pine Island.
review.objection: One agency source; the walk may overlap Murrumbidgee River Corridor candidates; climbing closed.

review.name: Majura Pines
review.reason: Mountain-bike trail network named by VisitCanberra cycling page (opened); a place riders go.
review.objection: One source, an activity venue in a plantation, overlap with Treetops/Majura area.

review.name: Changi Chapel
review.reason: Rule 2: small heritage chapel built by POWs at Changi, moved to Duntroon; Wikivoyage Canberra and North Canberra both name it (halfway along Miles Road) as military tourism, so a visitor source names a landmark. One listing, inside RMC Duntroon grounds.
review.objection: Short visit, one source repeated across two pages, sits inside Royal Military College grounds where most buildings are restricted; may be part of a Duntroon visit rather than a draw.

review.name: Royal Military College, Duntroon
review.reason: Wikivoyage: grounds open to the public (most buildings restricted), with Changi Chapel built by POWs on Miles Road (opened and read).
review.objection: Against: working military college, restricted buildings, one source. For: open grounds, a named chapel.

review.name: Duntroon Dairy
review.reason: Rule 3/2: Wikivoyage lists it as believed to be the oldest standing building in the ACT, viewable from a small car park with signage and lake views, but open only on request.
review.objection: Exterior view of about 15 minutes with one source; keeping adds a minor heritage stop. Against: no interior access.

review.name: Birrigai Time Trail
review.reason: Wikivoyage names a 3 km flat walk from the visitor centre to the Birrigai rock shelter (artefacts over 25,000 years old), a distinct Aboriginal heritage walk; I keep this as the trail and treat the shelter as its end. Single counted source seen.
review.objection: Against: one source, inside Tidbinbilla (already kept), and Wikivoyage's own claim of 'world's oldest inhabited rock shelter' is unverified. For: it is the reserve's one cultural-heritage visit and a guide singles it out.

review.name: Orroral Valley Tracking Station
review.reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi page lists the former NASA Earth station on Orroral Rd and it starts the Orroral Valley Circuit; single counted source
review.objection: For: a space-history stop in the same valley as Orroral Homestead. Against: ruins with little to see, one source, short visit.

review.name: Australian Alps Walking Track
review.reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'Do' names the northernmost section; long cross-border trail, only the northern end lies in the ACT (rule: long tracks are review).
review.objection: Not a place with one visit; most of the 640 km is in NSW/Vic and the ACT stretch is a remote leg through Namadgi.

review.name: Mount Gingera
review.reason: One counted source (Parks ACT walking tracks page, via leads; not opened - blocks scripts): 14.5 km return summit walk, peak a source names.
review.objection: Long full-day walk with one agency mention and no guide write-up; Wikivoyage does not list it.

review.name: Mount Franklin (Australian Capital Territory)
review.reason: Wikivoyage only mentions cross-country skiing there; the other counted source is the Namadgi tracks page on parks.act.gov.au (blocked, not read). Remote summit walk with Franklin Shelter.
review.objection: Case for: named summit walk with historic shelter. Against: remote, one thin source I could read, part of Namadgi National Park.

review.name: Orroral Valley Circuit
review.reason: Parks ACT walking tracks (via leads): 19 km day loop from the Orroral tracking station site.
review.objection: A full-day loop passing the homestead and tracking station, which are separate stops; one source.

review.name: Ginini Flats Wetlands Ramsar Site
review.reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See' names it: the ACT's only Ramsar wetland; one counted source.
review.objection: Reached only by high-country tracks; one line of description and little to see beyond the walk.

review.name: Hospital Hill Lookout
review.reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi lists the Boboyan Road lookout with interpretive signs and mountain views (opened); not a hospital.
review.objection: Against: roadside pull-out, one source. For: a guide names it.

review.name: Bendora Dam
review.reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See' (and Wikipedia): 1961 arch dam, first of its type in Australia, with lookouts.
review.objection: Remote and a single source; a dam wall viewed from a lookout.

review.name: Corin Dam
review.reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See' lists it (entry has no text); Corin Dam Road area is a recognised picnic and walking stop, but the visitor source says nothing of what to do.
review.objection: Empty listing; the area is better sourced as Corin Forest, an operator.

review.name: Cotter Dam
review.reason: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong and Country ACT (counted per candidate; I could not locate the listing text) and Wikipedia note a dam-wall viewing platform and picnics; a short, accessible stop.
review.objection: Mostly a water-supply dam; sourcing is thin and recreation is mostly the Cotter picnic areas.

review.name: Bendora Arboretum
review.reason: Wikivoyage Namadgi 'See': 1940 experimental plantings, 52 species, 5 km grade-2 walk.
review.objection: Wikivoyage itself calls it isolated and desolate, a 90-minute drive, so few visitors.

review.name: Cotter Reserve
review.reason: Parks ACT: the Cotter Recreation Area (river picnicking and swimming) that locals call the Cotter; the one name for the cluster of Cotter sites.
review.objection: An area with campground, avenue and bend as parts; Casuarina Sands overlaps.

review.name: Point Hut Crossing
review.reason: Parks ACT: shady Murrumbidgee crossing with sandy beaches, south end of the Discovery Track.
review.objection: A local picnic and walking stop; one source.

review.name: Uriarra Crossing
review.reason: Parks ACT: both banks of the Murrumbidgee, popular with birdwatchers.
review.objection: Local picnic area; one source.

review.name: Mugga-Mugga
review.reason: Wikivoyage lists the 1830s cottage with guided tours, but open only 10AM-2PM the first weekend of each month (opened and read).
review.objection: Against: not there whenever you arrive, one source, small. For: real heritage site with tours.

review.name: Geoscience Australia Education Centre
review.reason: Wikivoyage: free geology displays of minerals, fossils, Mon-Fri 9-5 (opened and read); one source, a short visit.
review.objection: Against: government agency foyer, niche. For: free, weekday daily, something to see.

review.name: Aranda Bushland Nature Reserve
review.reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): named Frost Hollow to Forest Walk, 1-2 hours.
review.objection: Against: suburban bushland, one source, no guide singles it out. For: agency-named walk.

review.name: Molonglo River Reserve
review.reason: Agency Murrumbidgee/Molonglo page names it with walking tracks; one source, no specific sight named.
review.objection: Against: unspecific, one source. For: a named reserve with tracks.

review.name: Tharwa Sandwash
review.reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): scenic picnic area on the Murrumbidgee in Gigerline Nature Reserve; keep this and reject Gigerline as the container.
review.objection: Against: picnic area, one source. For: agency-named riverside stop near Tharwa.

review.name: Blue Range Hut
review.reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): historic hut in Lower Cotter Catchment; nothing in the lead says what there is to see or how to reach it.
review.objection: For: historic hut the agency names. Against: little to see, one source.

review.name: Tuggeranong Pines
review.reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): riding and walking forest in Canberra's south.
review.objection: For: used for mountain biking and walking. Against: a plantation, one source.

review.reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): Japanese garden with lantern in Lennox Gardens on the lake; part of Lennox Gardens District Park.
review.objection: Against: small, one source, a garden inside a district park. For: distinct themed garden.

review.name: Canberra Beijing Garden
review.reason: parks.act.gov.au agency list (parks-act-leads.json, relied on): Chinese garden in Lennox Gardens on the lake, a distinct garden from Nara Peace Park.
review.objection: Against: small, one source, near-neighbour of Nara Peace Park. For: distinct garden.

pin_notes: All coordinates are hints from the enumerators (Wikipedia, Wikivoyage listing geo tags, OSM nodes) and must be re-resolved with resolve-pin.py (HIGH or MEDIUM) before apply. Spots with null coordinates need a pin: Anzac Parade, Murrumbidgee Discovery Track, Canberra Centenary Trail (loop midpoint), Weston Park (the candidate coordinates were Weston Park in England and were discarded), Goorooyarroo, Calthorpes' House, St John the Baptist Church, Hall, Casuarina Sands, Yankee Hat, Settlers Track, Jerrabomberra West Grasslands. Do not take Mount Ainslie, Black Mountain or the Tharwa point from a town page.
